dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "All 17 annual (365-day) recharges posted 2026-05-31 belong only to DLR-104 (8) and DLR-219 (9); totals/dates match dealer_import_log's DF-00020/DF-00040 exactly ($723.42/$782.87, 0.0 diff)"
"Zero subscribers in 24,542 rows have overlapping coverage periods (next renewal before prior term ends)"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31-May cluster is a contractually permitted monthly batch file from two dealers (DLR-104, DLR-219)"
"the effective/posted lag is isolated to two dealers with a documented monthly-file arrangement"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "No 'region' field exists; 'West' relies solely on the email naming these dealers."
"Data confirms DealerDrop's internal reconciliation, not dealer-side POS timestamps, so back-dating before upload can't be fully excluded."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Request DLR-104/DLR-219's original POS timestamps for the 17 May annual renewals to corroborate effective_event_date independently of DealerDrop"
"Flag their batch postings for separate treatment in the weekly trend pack."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Recommend closing as a reporting-timing item, not revenue-integrity."
"Evidence that would change this: any overlap or cash/ledger mismatch found on re-run with dealer POS data."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "contractually permitted" is stronger than the cited email evidence unless the underlying contracts were reviewed; the email supports the arrangement as reported, not necessarily its formal contractual approval.

"the test that catches double-billing even when totals reconcile" overstates what a coverage-overlap test establishes: it detects overlapping terms, but not every possible duplicate or erroneous charge.

"no revenue jump at the batching switch, no seasonal spike, so batching wasn't used to pad volume" is suggestive rather than dispositive evidence against manipulated reporting; matching cash and ledger can reproduce a shared upstream error.
"every other dealer and every 30/90-day plan posts same-day, all year" should be supported by a reproducible row-level lag analysis or query, rather than only the summary assertion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate billing, manipulated reporting, pipeline defects, and an innocent posting-time explanation. The strongest residual alternative is an upstream or dealer-side timestamp problem: effective dates could have been back-dated before upload, or the internal reconciliation could faithfully reconcile an incorrect source file. The submission acknowledges this but does not independently test it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide reproducible row-level tests or query outputs for the 17 affected events and the full posting-lag distribution, including source_event_id uniqueness, cash/ledger reconciliation, coverage overlap, and effective_event_date versus original POS timestamps; moderate the conclusion from high confidence/closure to conditional closure pending that corroboration.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South ticket volume fell post-10-May, but IVR-origin tickets stayed flat (12.1->12.9/wk); AGENT_DIRECT/APP/DEALER fell 35-75%"
"Of 487 NOVA-S1 sessions reaching issue_menu (attempting to report a problem), 341 (70%) ended ABANDONED/ERROR; TRANSFERRED collapsed from ~49% (legacy) to 3.3%"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The South ticket decline is largely a reporting-visibility artifact of the pilot's authentication gate, not proof self-service resolved more issues."
"Sessions ending before authentication are excluded from CareDesk case reporting entirely"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Confidence: High that the current metric overstates impact; Low-Medium on the true customer-experience effect either way."
"Unknowns: whether abandoned/errored callers re-contact via another channel that also isn't ticketing them (silent churn risk); true CSAT/NPS for pilot vs legacy callers - absent from this data."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally on this evidence."

"Pull CareDesk case-creation logic to confirm no case is opened for issue_menu sessions ending in ERROR/ABANDONED, and re-run the region comparison after authentication reliability is fixed, before any national expansion decision is made. Reversible; doesn't touch the live pilot."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What is the authentication failure/timeout rate for South NOVA-S1 sessions, and has it changed week-over-week since launch?"
"For a session ending in ERROR or ABANDONED at the issue_menu stage, what happens to that customer next - is any case, callback, or flag created anywhere?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the underlying problem rate did not improve" is stronger than the evidence supports: a slight rise in service events does not by itself measure the underlying complaint rate or customer friction.
"NO_SIGNAL (self-service can't fix)" treats the issue type as categorically outside self-service scope without showing that all such cases could not be resolved through the pilot.

"The South ticket decline is largely a reporting-visibility artifact" is plausible and well supported, but the submission has not yet directly verified the case-creation rule or linked failed journeys to subsequent outcomes.

"re-run the region comparison after authentication reliability is fixed" presumes authentication reliability is the relevant fix before the proposed case-creation and sampled-journey checks establish that mechanism.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the main benign alternatives that fewer tickets could reflect fewer real problems or successful IVR absorption, and explicitly preserved uncertainty about recontacts and customer satisfaction. It missed a fully tested interpretation that many ABANDONED sessions may reflect non-complaint intent, caller choice, or successful resolution outside CareDesk; service-event counts and IVR outcomes alone cannot distinguish those possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link issue_menu ERROR/ABANDONED sessions to downstream cases, repeat contacts, callbacks, and sampled call recordings, including a comparable LEGACY cohort, before asserting that the decline is primarily a capture failure.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: "INV-09's TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED (2026-06-04) has no prior fault/alarm event for INV-09 anywhere in this file" is tied to inverter_events.csv and INV-09 rows.
"Every row is severity info/warning, cleared=yes, impact_mw=0" is explicitly tied to a full-column scan of inverter_events.csv.
The small-sample qualification is stated alongside the claim that the file contains 4 events across 9 days.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes the missing onset from a plant failure and proposes two plausible innocent explanations: "the export window may be truncated" or "this event type is emitted independently of an onset record."
It cross-checks status, severity, MW impact, recurrence, event count, and date span rather than relying only on the TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED label.
The recommended source-system check directly tests whether the apparent anomaly is a logging/schema behavior.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The file-size limitation is explicitly acknowledged: "may be a filtered extract, not the full log."
The submission limits its conclusion to the supplied data: "nothing here indicates ongoing malfunction from the data itself."
It asks for a small, decision-relevant check rather than asserting that the missing onset proves a fault or proves a logging defect.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: "Perform one cheap check, don't escalate" follows from cleared=yes, impact_mw=0, non-recurring events, and the absence of an active fault indication.
The proposed checks are discriminating: verify event-pairing semantics and verify whether the file is complete or pre-filtered.
The action preserves the legitimate quality check without creating an unsupported operational escalation.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the result: "Nothing in the file as given warrants escalation."
It captures the supported operational picture: all four events are cleared, have zero recorded MW impact, and do not recur on a single inverter.
It avoids inventing a plant problem from a small communications/event export and stops after identifying one cheap follow-up.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No pattern of recurring or escalating faults visible in this sample" is reasonable but cannot rule out recurrence outside the supplied file; the submission appropriately qualifies the limited sample and possible filtering.

"Rejected: every event is already cleared with zero recorded MW impact" does not prove that no underlying equipment issue ever occurred; it supports only that the supplied export shows no active unresolved impact. The conclusion itself is appropriately scoped to the file.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The missing INV-09 onset may be a normal event-model behavior or an artifact of a truncated/pre-filtered export, rather than evidence of an inverter fault. A separate possibility is that the source system omitted or retained the onset outside the export window; both interpretations are left open and are directly testable.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the source-system check explicitly verify the event schema and exact time-window boundaries: determine whether TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED normally has a paired onset, then confirm whether INV-09's preceding interval and any excluded event types were included in the export.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv and specific fields, blocks, times, and rupee totals: “Only blocks 53-64 (13:00-16:00) used schedule_source=pilot_revision” and “penalty was 19.6% higher on 29-May (Rs 439,011) than 28-May (Rs 366,914).”
It also distinguishes the arithmetic result from causal evidence: “The 31.6% DSM-penalty reduction is arithmetically reproducible ... but is not evidence the pilot reduced penalty.”
However, it does not use the required same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw comparison on 29-May, leaving the central pilot-effect estimate unexamined.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests a plausible confound by noting “Mean wind speed in the pilot window was higher on 29-May (10.27 vs 9.01 m/s).”
It correctly observes that the 84 non-pilot blocks used qca_base on both days and that the day-level improvement cannot automatically be attributed to a scheduling method.

But it treats a cross-day pilot-window comparison as evidence about pilot performance: “its own active hours performed worse.” That comparison is confounded by day and wind conditions, and the submission does not perform the same-day counterfactual required by the supplied materials.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately states “Causally unidentified” and identifies uncertainty about “forecast accuracy, cloud cover, unmodeled factors.”
It proposes multiple matched high-wind days and same-day A/B testing, showing awareness that the single day is insufficient.

Nevertheless, “if anything, its own active hours performed worse” and “the improvement is entirely in non-pilot hours” are stronger than warranted as causal interpretations because the active-hour comparison is across different days and omits the same-day schedule counterfactual.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot for data collection only; do not expand or claim savings based on this comparison” is a proportionate response to weak causal identification.
The proposed next measurement—“pilot-revision vs qca_base scheduling within the same day and similar stow windows across multiple high-wind days”—is directionally discriminating.
It should first require analysis of the available 29-May same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw counterfactual, rather than relying primarily on future paired days.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly rejects the headline claim as a controlled causal estimate: “this single day does not show the pilot reduced DSM exposure.”

However, it overcorrects by implying the pilot had no demonstrated benefit and by characterizing its active hours as worse based on a different-day comparison. The supplied same-day counterfactual supports retaining a smaller, nonzero pilot-day benefit while rejecting the 31.6% causal attribution.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The full-day improvement comes entirely from the other 84 blocks, where both days used identical qca_base scheduling - a 95.2% penalty drop unrelated to the pilot.” The arithmetic decomposition is supported, but “unrelated to the pilot” is a causal conclusion not established by identical schedule_source labels alone.
“If anything, its own active hours performed worse.” The reported 19.6% cross-day increase is observed, but it does not isolate the pilot effect because the days and wind conditions differ.

“This single day does not show the pilot reduced DSM exposure” is too broad if read as denying any same-day pilot-day benefit; it is defensible only as a statement that the day-level 31.6% reduction is not causally identified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 28-to-29 May full-day comparison does not identify a 31.6% pilot-caused reduction, but the 29-May same-day comparison of base_schedule_mw against submitted_schedule_mw indicates a smaller pilot-day benefit. The appropriate conclusion is limited evidence of operational value, not proof of the headline causal effect and not evidence of no value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Analyze the 29-May same-day counterfactual directly: compare penalty or deviation under base_schedule_mw with submitted_schedule_mw for the pilot-active blocks, then report that smaller effect separately from the uncontrolled 28-versus-29 May day-level comparison.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared CH code 90211000 differs from product master's Helios code 90211090 for P1001" with source "declaration.pdf vs product_master_current.xlsx"
"country_tariff_matrix.xlsx has no Switzerland rows; covers only EU member states" with source "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx"
"For EU states, P1001's approved code changed 90211010->90211090 on 1-Jul-2025; the CH filing (4-Nov-2025) matches neither EU variant"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Origin misdeclaration explains the flag": rejected - origin is US consistently across all three documents
"Helios reference is simply wrong": not supported - it matches the EU's current post-transition code for this product family, though its nomenclature basis for Switzerland is unconfirmed
"We cannot confirm 90211090 is the correct Swiss benchmark"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do not escalate as a confirmed declaration error; treat as unresolved pending Swiss-specific reference data"
The evidence table assigns "High" confidence to direct document comparisons, "Medium" confidence to the EU transition comparison, and identifies that the Swiss benchmark is "unconfirmed"
"Swiss national tariff schedule or ruling for HS 902110; confirmation of which nomenclature system 'Helios Commodity Code' represents; whether 90211000 is a valid legacy Swiss subheading"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx contains no Switzerland entries - only EU states (DE/FR/BE/ES/IE) on the EU Combined Nomenclature system"
"Switzerland is outside the EU and may use a distinct national subheading at the 8th digit despite sharing HS6 902110"
"For EU states, P1001's approved code changed 90211010->90211090 on 1-Jul-2025"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate as a confirmed declaration error"
"Request the Swiss customs tariff reference for HS 902110 and clarify the Helios field's nomenclature basis before deciding on escalation"
"no filing amendment yet"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that consistent US origin across three documents means there is "no origin mismatch" is supported as a documentary consistency finding, but it does not independently establish that the declared origin is factually correct.

The rejection of "Origin misdeclaration explains the flag" is reasonable as an explanation for this code discrepancy, but documentary agreement alone cannot fully rule out an underlying origin misdeclaration.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is that 90211000 is a valid Swiss national or legacy subheading and the Helios 90211090 value is an EU-derived benchmark that is not applicable to Switzerland; this would make the discrepancy a benign jurisdiction/code-system mismatch rather than a declaration error.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish documentary consistency from proof of factual origin and obtain the Swiss tariff or ruling to determine whether 90211000 is valid for the filing date.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "SUP-02/P1006's register entry (origin Ireland) expired 2025-07-31, before the invoice date; only SUP-02 was searched" — supplier_declaration_reference.txt, supplier_origin_register.csv
"SUP-01/P1006 has a current register entry (origin United States, Available, valid through 2025-12-31)" — supplier_origin_register.csv
"ClearView shows the preference indicator present but supplier support not linked" — review_note.txt

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "No supporting document exists anywhere": rejected - SUP-01/P1006 has a current, origin-matching record in the same register
"SUP-02 is confirmed as the shipment's supplier": rejected - nothing in the packet names an internal supplier_id
"whether SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025 is the document the broker intended to invoke" — Missing Evidence

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "cannot be confirmed or ruled out from current evidence"
"No document confirms which supplier actually shipped this consignment, so neither record can be assumed relevant without that link"
"do not contest the already-Accepted declaration on the current evidence"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "the specific gap found so far may be a wrong-supplier search rather than a missing document"
"the earlier search simply didn't check it"
"confirm the shipment's actual supplier via PO/sourcing records before treating this as unsupported"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Re-run the supplier-declaration search against SUP-01/P1006"
"confirm the shipment's actual supplier via PO/sourcing records"
"do not contest the already-Accepted declaration on the current evidence"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement "No document in this packet states which internal supplier_id sourced this specific shipment" is appropriately cautious but is supported only by the three named documents; it would be stronger if it identified the exact fields or passages reviewed.

The description of SUP-01 as "origin-matching" could be misread as proving preferential origin. The submission otherwise avoids that conclusion, but should explicitly state that matching declared manufacturing/origin data is not proof of preferential origin or supplier validity.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be supportable: SUP-01/P1006 has an available, in-date United States-origin register entry, and the missing linkage may be a search or data-lineage problem rather than absent supplier support. Conversely, the register entry alone does not establish that SUP-01 supplied this shipment or that the relevant preferential-origin rule was satisfied.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish the invoice's manufacturing country and the register's declared origin from preferential origin, then document the exact invoice, airway-bill, PO, and register fields or rows needed to link SUP-01 or SUP-02 to this consignment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185/262 rows have qcore_release_ts time-of-day = 02:10:00, matching source_snapshot_ts exactly" — specific field-level observation with a computed count.
"lab_complete_ts is sourced from LabTrack, 'an analytics extract, not live application,' refreshed only every 48h" — relevant freshness evidence is cited.
The submission does not explicitly identify that the QCore and LabTrack extracts are not a coherent point-in-time snapshot, limiting triangulation.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "strongly indicating these are nightly-batch-job stamps, not true disposition-event times" — develops a plausible timestamp-semantics mechanism from the concentration pattern.
"batch-pattern rows average 46.8h ... vs 38.4h for non-batch rows" — compares groups rather than relying only on the overall average.
The explanation does not fully separate interface-commit timing from actual workflow delay, and the argument that pure display rounding should produce similar group averages is not necessarily valid.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "strongly indicating" appropriately treats batch stamping as an inference, and the catalog definition is assigned "Medium" confidence.
"verify before using this as a KPI" recognizes decision-relevant uncertainty.

The conclusion that these are "not true disposition-event times" is stronger than the available evidence supports; a clustered interface timestamp could coexist with delayed or otherwise valid operational timing. Source freshness is noted but not fully incorporated into the uncertainty bounds.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Yes, verify before using this as a KPI" is a useful pause on KPI adoption.
"Smallest verification: pull the QCore data-catalog definition ... and spot-check ... against QCore's live audit trail" proposes a focused, reversible check.

"If it confirms batch-load semantics, cycle time must be computed at daily granularity only" is an unsafe or incomplete remediation: daily aggregation does not resolve whether the timestamp represents an interface commit, decision time, or workflow delay, and the SOP's required-evidence start point is not addressed.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The 1.5-day figure is just informal and roughly right": rejected" uses the observed overall average as counterevidence.
"This is normal daily-refresh rounding with no real distortion": not fully rejected but weakened" acknowledges an alternative rather than asserting certainty.

The strongest competing explanation—real workflow delay combined with interface or extract timing—is not explicitly tested, and no clear observation is stated that would revive or discriminate it beyond the catalog/audit check.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "pull the QCore data-catalog definition ... and spot-check a sample ... against QCore's live audit trail" is a small, high-value request targeted at timestamp semantics.
"lab_complete_ts needs the same check against LabTrack before any hour-level KPI is built" identifies a second relevant evidence gap.

The request could be more precise about obtaining event/decision timestamps or an event log and reconciling extract snapshot times, which would directly discriminate measurement artifact from workflow performance.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "strongly indicating these are nightly-batch-job stamps, not true disposition-event times" overstates what timestamp clustering alone proves; it supports a batch/interface-timing hypothesis, not necessarily the absence of valid operational timing.

"If it confirms batch-load semantics, cycle time must be computed at daily granularity only" is not sufficiently supported and could conceal the underlying timestamp-definition problem rather than solve it.
The comparison that pure display rounding should yield similar batch and non-batch averages is not a reliable rejection test without knowing the rounding rule and event-time distribution.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration may reflect an interface commit or scheduled extract rather than the actual disposition decision, while some of the apparent cycle time may still be genuine workflow delay. In addition, the LabTrack and QCore extracts may represent different snapshots, so the joined cycle-time averages may combine timing and snapshot artifacts.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the timestamp definition and a small event-level reconciliation containing required-evidence-available time, disposition/decision time, QCore interface-commit time, and extract snapshot times for sampled rows; use that result to decide whether the KPI should be redefined, not merely aggregated to daily granularity.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "available_qty_global is negative for 2 of 27 parts despite positive on_hand" — spare_parts.csv; "MaintStar-global snapshot is 2026-06-26" — source_freshness.csv; "RI-0001 and ME-0003 ... reserved_for_critical_asset=true" — part_restrictions.csv

The submission identifies specific part numbers, quantities, files, dates, and restriction fields, and triangulates requests, stock, restrictions, policy, and freshness. It does not provide row-level detail for every value or fully substantiate the percentage calculations.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Semantic matching itself works well here" but "restriction and revision data (not description) block or complicate roughly 83% of the value."
"available_qty_global ... proving this lag is real, not theoretical."

It separates retrieval similarity from transferability and tests reservation, revision, pooled quantity, and freshness explanations. However, negative global availability alongside positive on-hand demonstrates inconsistency, not conclusively that refresh lag is the cause; commitments, timing, or differing definitions remain possible.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Needs check" and "Actionable-pending-one-cheap-live-check, not actionable outright"
"given the availability-feed lag applies to all matches equally."

The submission uses claim-specific categories and recognizes the stale global snapshot, but the assertion that lag applies equally to all matches and the claim that it is proven are stronger than the evidence warrants.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Semantic search as candidate generation" is operationally reflected by classifying candidates as "Not transferable," "Needs check," or pending live verification.
"A live MaintStar ... or ERP query for the specific pump-seal and valve-actuator candidates" and an Engineering revision ruling are proposed as focused next actions.

The recommendation avoids treating semantic matches as automatic transfers, protects against reservation and revision risks, and proposes small, reversible checks that can convert candidates into actionable decisions.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Sum of all matched external quotes = realizable savings": rejected"
"Description mismatches are the only barrier": rejected"

The submission tests two plausible leadership interpretations against reservation, revision, quantity, and freshness evidence. It does not fully develop the strongest alternative explanation for the global/local discrepancy, such as different stock-versus-commitment definitions or extract timing.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live MaintStar (not the monthly global extract) or ERP query for the specific pump-seal and valve-actuator candidates"
"a revision-equivalence ruling from Engineering on VLV-3722 RevA vs RevB"

The requested evidence is narrow, prioritized, and directly tied to decisions. It could be stronger by specifying which query fields or success criteria would establish true free stock, UOM, qualification, and reservation release.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "proving this lag is real, not theoretical" is overstated: negative global availability with positive on-hand proves a discrepancy but does not by itself identify refresh lag as the cause.

"the availability-feed lag applies to all matches equally" is insufficiently supported without confirming that every candidate relies on the same extract and that local availability definitions are comparable.
The percentage range "9.7-17.3% ... pump seals, +other categories" is imprecise and not transparently reconciled to the stated category totals.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The global negative quantities may reflect commitments, reservations, or a different availability definition rather than only a stale snapshot. Under that interpretation, some candidates could be unavailable even after a live refresh, while others may be locally transferable if the live system confirms unreserved, qualified, revision-compatible stock.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run one targeted live query for each proposed pump-seal and valve-actuator transfer showing part identity, revision, UOM, qualification, unrestricted quantity, reservations, and last-update time, then reconcile those results to the monthly global extract; this would discriminate stale-data risk from genuine lack of free stock and convert candidate value into an actionable value estimate.
